newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal PM sees 1996 GDP growth near 2.75 percent.
newsitem.headline: Portugal PM sees 1996 GDP growth near 2.75 percent.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said 1996 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth should be very close to 2.75 percent.
"We shall have a GDP growth rate this year very close to that foreseen by the government, which was 2.75 percent," he told a lunch attended by Portuguese industrialists.
In 1995, GDP grew by 2.2 percent, according to central bank figures.
"The confidence indicators are far from desirable, but there are (positive) signals in mortgage credit and consumption," Guterres said.
"There is very worrying stagnation in the manufacturing industry," he added.
Antonio de Sousa, governor of the Bank of Portugal, was quoted as saying in last Saturday's Expresso weekly that 1996 GDP growth should stand at between 2.25 and 2.75 percent.
